title: Identification of potential inflammatory breast cancer biomarkers by comprehensive TGIRT-seq profiling of RNAs in tumor and blood samples
description: Inflammatory breast cancer (IBC) is the most lethal breast cancer subtype, but lags in biomarker identification due to lack of large, discrete tumors. Here, we used TGIRT-seq to comprehensively profile coding and non-coding RNAs in tumors, PBMCs, and plasma from IBC and non-IBC patients and healthy donors. Besides RNAs from known IBC-relevant genes, we identified hundreds of other over-expressed coding and non-coding RNAs in IBC (p<=0.001), including subsets with elevated intron-to-exon depth ratios (IDRs) that may result from enhanced transcription resulting in accumulation of unspliced pre-mRNAs. Potential IBC biomarkers in plasma included T-cell receptor pre-mRNA fragments traced to IBC tumors and PBMCs; intron RNA fragments correlated with high IDR genes; and RNA fragments from LINE-1 and other retroelements, which are globally activated in IBC. Our findings provide new insights into IBC, define a new bioinformatic parameter relevant to RNA splicing, and demonstrate advantages of broadly analyzing transcriptomes for biomarker identification.
